name: FPSO and floating production structures
principle: Floating production systems keep process plant on a floating hull: converted tankers or newbuild FPSOs, semi-submersibles or spar hulls, held by moorings or dynamic positioning. Turret-moored FPSOs weathervane into the environment with a swivel stack carrying fluids, power and signals; spread-moored units suit calm or unidirectional seas. Hull design, station-keeping, riser and umbilical dynamics, and motion effects on process equipment (sloshing, level control, rotating equipment limits) define the engineering.

process_steps.name: Hull built or converted with topsides integration
Mooring system designed, pre-laid and hooked up
Risers and umbilicals connected, flexible or rigid
Production, offloading and ballast operations managed around weather

performance.basis: MODEC FPSO Projects experience page states 59 units in 20 countries (delivered/operated fleet)

source.note: MODEC home, FPSO Projects experience, read 2026-11-07

limitations: motion, sloshing and fatigue limit equipment choices and inspection access
mooring integrity over 20-25 year service is a monitored, classed lifetime obligation
advantages: no fixed infrastructure left after field life — FPSOs disconnect and redeploy
wellhead and storage combined; works where building platforms is uneconomic
